## What it is

The organization-wide plan for the information security program, covering every element SP 800-53 PM-1 requires, with the program management and common controls the organization provides.

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-1 requires an organization-wide information security program plan that gives an overview of the program's requirements, describes the program management and common controls that meet them, assigns roles, and is approved by a senior official. NIST publishes no outline for this plan, so the sections below follow the elements of PM-1a in order, and each cites the item it meets. The plan can be one document or a set of documents, as long as this plan names the set. It describes how the organization defends itself, so restrict access to it (PM-1c).
:::

| Organization | Plan version | Approved by | Approval date | Next review |

### 1. Purpose and scope

This plan describes <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>'s information security program: the requirements it meets, the program management and common controls that meet them, and who is responsible for each (PM-1a.1).

It applies to all of <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>: <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: the organizational units, locations and mission and business functions the program covers</span>. The systems in scope are listed in the system inventory (PM-5).

### 6. Compliance and performance

- Compliance with the security policies is checked through control assessments and continuous monitoring, following the continuous monitoring strategy (PM-31).
- Exceptions to policy are requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with compensating measures in <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: where exceptions are recorded</span>.
- Violations are handled through the organization's sanctions process.

| Plan of action and milestones items past their due date | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: target</span> | Plans of action and milestones |
| Vulnerabilities remediated within the required times | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: target</span> | Vulnerability scanning |
| Personnel with current security awareness training | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: target</span> | Training records |

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal agencies, this plan documents the agency-wide information security program required by the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554(b)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim)). The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is the senior agency information security officer designated under 44 U.S.C. § 3554(a)(3)(A), and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> is the Senior Agency Official for Privacy designated under [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf).

- Section 2 shall list the federal laws, OMB policies and CISA directives that apply to the agency's systems. (PM-1a.1)

</div>
